The game sets you within a terminal at an unknown place and with a gun in your hand. You have no idea who you are and have to explore the world and figure out various puzzles to figure it all out.

A preview was released in 2014, and it is simply stunning in its execution. The 3D effect and scaling as you move around, makes it feel like a game built in Unity/Unreal engine and with a fixed camera angle. It’s extremely well done and looks quite unlike any C64 game i’ve seen before.

Engine wise it seems to be quite advance, and I assume that all was left was mostly the content of the game to finish off. We’re not sure if it has indeed been cancelled, or just put on hold for now. Certainly we hope the latter.

210582.overview: A single player SEUCK based Shoot'em Up by Richard Bayliss. Blubba is trapped in a nightmare and unfortunately for him, he has to make an escape. The world is guarded by various demons and monsters and Blubba has to defeat the Imaginator. Good luck, you WILL need it.

213670.overview:
Ice Titans is a shooter for the C64 that is somewhat loosely inspired by Jeff Minter's Laser Zone, albeit scaled down.

Ice Titans is the game to play if you're looking for a real break out. The gameplay is simple and easy to figure out:
shoot everything that moves.

During your expedition into the eternal ice, you woke up a couple of the natives of the same. And they're not exactly happy about your intrusion.

You control the two cannons with the joystick in port 2 .

If you get caught, the game starts again. Otherwise you can advance to the next higher and therefore more difficult level. 

It was developed by Cleveland M. Blakemore and originally published in Ahoy! 1988/01 (Issue #49), but was later published in Magic Disk 64  1988/08.

214618.overview: A logical puzzle game developed by John Christian Lønningdal (coding) and Saul Cross (graphics and SFX/music)  for the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2015/2016. It was released into the public domain on April 1, 2016.

214716.overview:
Trap your dinner by moving boulders to guide chickens to your cooking pot.

The game was developed by Frank Mikulastik for Funfare House, Inc. and published by CBS College Publishing as a type-in game in the book "Arcade Games for the Commodore 64" in 1985.

215119.overview:
Interlox is a simple, yet effective game based on the old children's favorite, Noughts & Crosses/Tic-Tac-Toe.

It differs from that game only in the fact that it is played not on one 3x3 square, but on 4-interlocking squares simultaneously.

Interlox may be played by one player against the computer, or by two players against each other.

For convenience, the board is laid out in the same format as the C64 keyboard; each position on the board is selected by hitting the appropriate key.


One Player Game:

The player must make as many lines of three counters as possible, horizontal, vertical, or diagonal, withine any of the four squares.

At the same time, he, or she must prevent the C64 from making a line.


Two Player Game:

Each player takes it in turn to place their counters on the board.

The winner is the one with the highest score when the board is full.

The game was developed by Australian coder, Barry "Cout Games" Hart and released into the public domain in 2018.

The game is also an unofficial conversion of an old type-in game for the Commodore VIC-20.

215650.overview:
At the local meet of the Birmingham Adventure Players Society you discussed the usual adventure related topics as you always do at these meetings. 
"What I would like is to play a REAL adventure!"
Lizzie, your best friend, said, "Really? Well maybe we can fix that!" she smiled, her usual sarcastic grin spread across her face.
"Ya! I believe that when I see it!" you replied.
"My aunt has an old house just outside Birmingham. How do you fancy playing a REAL adventure in that old house? She is away on holiday for a couple of weeks and I'm sure I can put something together for you."
"Oh yeah! I won't be the subject of another of your practical jokes!"
"You coward! You're scared!"
"I'm not!"
"Do it then! I DARE YOU!"
And so the challenge began. Lizzie needed a week to prepare everything and now that week was over!

215652.overview: A one or two player SEUCK based Shoot'em Up created and published by Outlaw-Emix Software included simultaneous co-operative play. Ride your motorized ski-bike around shooting the rival ice tribesmen, the zeppelins, balloons and other hazards. Watch out for lurkers in the tents, they will make your life in-tents! Dodge bears and bats and penguins all with a taste for snowcones of blood!

215654.overview: A German language science fiction RPG game. The aim was to guide a party of 4 characters through a mission, which was divided into three levels. The screen arrangement was as in Ultima. There were lots of sounds and little graphics and lots of features mentioned. The aim of the game is to reactivate a central computer console in the space city, the Triton 5 gas mine colony. Initially, however, the player and three companions are on board a cargo cruiser and must first ensure that the ship is in place. Achieved objective and landed on the colony. After possibly stocking up on some gear, you might want to consider leaving the ship and getting what you need in the colony, eventually stepping in front of the central computer console. From time to time it may seem convenient to contact the Ministry of Internal Affairs on Drabamp and get some assistance from them, but other than that the player is on their own.

215655.overview:
ISS Emergency! is an official conversion of a ZX Spectrum text adventure of the same name (also released earlier in the same year)
Like the original Spectrum version, the C64 conversion was also developed by John Whatson & Gareth Pitchford and released in 2019.

216285.overview: Originally programmed by Ari Laakkonen in 1983 and published in a floppy magazine two years later, The Island is a text adventure where your goal is to find and collect pieces of treasure hidden around the island.

217113.overview: It's Magic (not to be confused with the public domain game from Protovision's public domain label) is a miscellaneous action/platform game. It was developed by Stefan Muth and published in 64'er 1991/11. Magic doesn't get you very far in this game by Stefan Muth, even if the title might suggest so. Rather, a reaction and a portion of desire are required here. The task is to bring back a lost amulet to a magician. The problem with this is that this magician lives in a penthouse on the 28th floor, and there are six elevators on each floor. One of these blinks, and now the amulet has to be moved to it with the help of the joystick. Now simply press the (fire) button. A new elevator will blink, so it's up and down the first level 20 times. Sounds pretty easy so far, almost too easy.

217114.overview: It's About Time is an educational game that aims to teach young children about time and how time/clocks work. The game was developed and published by Micrograms, Inc. in 1986.

218807.overview: Insect Jungle is a French language Centipede clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by a Josselin Chenet and published in the following: Hebdogiciel N°142 (04.07.1986) + N°143 (11.07.1986) + N°144 (18.07.1986). Fight fiercely against the vermin crawling in your Commodore as a result of an obvious lack of maintenance, you'll need to make the best use of your joystick (in port 2) for controlled cleaning.

219849.overview:
The hillbilly restaurants need your help. Their customers are hungry and impatient, so get in the kitchen and start making sandwiches!

Make sandwiches that match the pictures at the top of the screen. Click on the ingredients as they scroll by to drop them onto the conveyor belts and then onto the plates at the bottom.

You can build the sandwiches on the conveyor belts and on the plates. The ingredients don't have to be in the same order as the pictures, but each sandwich must contain the correct ingredients. The more ingredients you get in the right order, the more you will score.

220042.overview:
Impulse is another sideways scrolling shooter, has titles in place and a main ship that you can shoot enemies with. However, the attack waves are endless, as is the repeating background – but it is a promising start to a title which would have been well suited to a budget label of the time.

Of course – nothing ever surfaced and the game remained unreleased.

220127.overview:
Dagon’s Awakening by Vintage Computing Carinththia was released physically in the limited edition Underwater Collection - Deluxe LED&Sound Cartridge. It had its first debut at Vintage Computing Carinthia $1F.  
 
In this game, you take on the role of a member of the Esoteric Order of Dagon who is on his way to perform a ritual to awaken Dagon, a giant ancient with a visage enough to drive mortals insane.

The setting is inspired by the stories of H.P. Lovecraft and the game has several endings. Enjoy!

278182.overview:
Title Reference: The title comes from a line from the character Ralph Wiggum which is seen on The Simpsons from the episode This Little Wiggy from Season 9, Episode 18.

About the Game:

The object of the game is to pick your nose to find ‘moon rocks’. You can pick from either your left or right nostril at anytime. The more you pick, the more points you score! However, don’t pick too much, or you will get a nosebleed!

Released as part of Reset Magazine's 2018 C64 4KB Craptastic Game Coding Competition.

417884.overview: In this odd take on games like Kaboom, your goal is either to drop a deuce in the toilet on the bottom of the screen, or to play as the toilet and catch the turds as they fall. The game was developed by Sasha Stojanovic and released into the public domain in 2011.

418521.overview: A labyrinth\maze action game by Logiker and released at the  Vintage Computing Carinthia $20: "32nd VCC Meeting" on the Back On Black Fun Compo disk.

418697.overview:
International Skoda Racin'n'Bashin	is a shoot 'em up game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Richard Bayliss using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit and published by Binary Zone PD in 1995.

The game was an attempt to make a "Spy Hunter" like game using SEUCK.

418703.overview:
International Skoda Racin'n'Bashin II is the sequel to the original game. Like the original, it is an attempt to make a "Spy Hunter" like game on the Commodore 64 using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit (SEUCK) Just like the original, it was developed by Richard Bayliss.  

The sequel does feature improved graphics over the original game.

It was published by Binary Zone PD in 1997.

425141.overview: Players control paddles and bounce the puck setting it in motion at different speeds and directions. A point is reached when the puck hits the player's or opponent's goal. The game ends after a certain amount of time or when one player reaches the maximum number of points.

425443.overview: Infinirail is a stock market trading simulation developed by Jeroen Gildemacher and released in on July 1, 2022 as part of the 2022 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition.

425533.overview: Impetus is a simple vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Japanese coder Inufuto and released into the public domain in 2021.

447080.overview: The game makes the process of the possible successors of the 8-bit generation playable, both of which came onto the market in 1985: Atari ST (Cheap and initially widely available) and the Amiga gaming machine (similarly priced from 1987/88 with the Amiga 500). These two systems and their fans fought a tough battle: which was the better system? A real war of identity. This "war" is made playable as a duel game with the corresponding logos through 12 levels. This culture war ends with the victory of the consoles and a little later with new, inexpensive PCs and 3D graphics cards.

448473.overview: Take on the role of Iowa Jack - adventurer, tomb raider and pilot for hire - and head off in search of a legendary treasure in this old school text adventure game.

448604.overview: It is the year 2037, contact with the scientific base on IO has been lost. you must discover what happened. 452374.overview: Milano, 1999. A mysterious car crash takes the life of entrepreneur Victor Erni. 463682.overview:
A life simulation game published in the Italian book "20 Programmi per Commodore 64". 
 
Come to know the harsh rules of survival. We know, in fact, that too few "individuals" lead to a species' extinction due to reproductive difficulties, while too many trigger natural selection—eliminating the weakest individuals, for instance, because there isn't enough food for everyone. There is, however, a point of equilibrium that allows a relatively stable number of individuals to survive and reproduce. Our program will simulate this simple natural law by representing a "territory" on the screen (imagine, for example, the hunting grounds of a prehistoric tribe) and allowing the player to place a certain number of stars within it (representing the inhabitants): depending on the number of stars placed, the system will identify a state of overpopulation, under-population, or equilibrium based on established parameters. Starting from the player's initial configuration, the program will calculate a second "generation" of stars (i.e., the number of individuals remaining in the territory after one generation, according to the law of survival) and all subsequent generations, until a command is issued to stop execution. Since the population a territory can sustain varies according to social and technological conditions, the reader can modify the size of the territory and the parameters determining the birth and death rates of the stars (representing the individuals) by making very simple changes to a few lines of the program.
